what_worked: Data-quality caveat on the 56% untagged MRR is genuinely useful and disciplines every downstream claim.
fix_next: Total revenue is $15.6M not $13.47M; conflating MRR with 30-day revenue corrupts the headline number and cascading percentages throughout.
verdict: Strong strategic narrative undermined by a core revenue definition error.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2/3: States total MRR is $13.47M—the dataset's total 30-day revenue is $15,596,344.59; the deck appears to have subtracted something or used a different field without explanation. Slide 2/5: Top-10 share stated as 48%—reference is 49.6%. Slide 2: 'Stan is 26.5%'—reference says anonymous companies are 12.9% of companies and 26.525% of revenue, but attributing this to a single named account 'Stan' is unverifiable and likely conflates anonymous cohort with one entity. Slide 8: AI median stated as $446—reference is $503; Education median $2,142 vs reference $2,435; Marketing median not shown but other medians diverge. Slide 10: B2B median stated as $1,036 and B2C $181, giving 5.7x ratio—reference shows median revenue multiples of 2.35x/2.30x, far from 5.7x. Slide 7: AI total revenue shown as $1,806K—reference is $2,356,676; SaaS shown as $589K vs reference $703K. Slide 12: Stripe share stated as 87.2% of MRR—reference shows Stripe revenue $13.53M out of $15.6M total = 86.7%, close but the denominator confusion propagates.

evidence.insight: Slide 6 data-quality finding about 56% untagged MRR is original and decision-useful. Slide 9 portfolio matrix and slide 13 white-space analysis synthesize multiple dimensions. Slide 15 prioritization framework ties findings to actions with effort/value axes.
evidence.narrative: Clear five-finding thesis on slide 2 carried through concentration (slide 5), data quality (slide 6), category (slides 7-9), B2B/B2C (slide 10), infrastructure (slide 12), risk (slide 14), and recommendations (slides 15-16). Each slide builds on prior. Strong landing.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 states audience (senior leadership), scope (1,000-listing sample), and date. Slide 6 explicitly scopes category analysis to 44% of MRR. Slide 14 acknowledges data incompleteness. Limitations are handled better than most decks.
evidence.accuracy: Core revenue figure ($13.47M vs $15.6M) is wrong or at minimum unexplained—the deck uses both numbers but treats $13.47M as 'total MRR' and $15.6M as '30-day revenue run-rate' as if they're different metrics, when the dataset has one 30-day revenue field. Category totals on slide 7 are systematically lower than reference. B2B/B2C median ratio of 5.7x contradicts reference 2.35x. Multiple median values diverge from reference.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme, clear hierarchy with section labels, well-annotated charts. Bubble chart on slide 9 is somewhat cluttered with overlapping labels. Pie chart on slide 12 is acceptable but not ideal. Y-axis labels on slide 9 are truncated. Overall professional and restrained.
evidence.ai_slop: Consulting-style language ('cash cow', 'stars', 'watch list') is formulaic but grounded in actual data. Prioritization matrix on slide 15 is a standard framework applied reasonably. No decorative-but-meaningless graphics. Minimal slop overall.
